task: Split conformal (nominal 90%) for binary risk-difference contrasts, FULL v2 feature set, HistGBT point model (models_eval.fit_gbt), sigma = HistGBT on |residual|.

recipes.split: 50/50 trial-grouped split of training pool (GroupShuffleSplit seed 0); q = ceil((n+1)(1-a))/n quantile of |cal residual|; normalized sigma fit on proper-train in-sample |residuals| (compressed scale, sigma_cut ~0.02 reflects this), rescaled by conformal q on the calibration half.
recipes.crossfit: 5-fold GroupKFold over training pool; out-of-fold residuals for all pool rows; sigma cross-fitted (fold-k sigma trained on other folds' OOF |res|); q from n_pool normalized OOF residuals; final point and sigma models refit on whole pool (CV+-style, not strictly exchangeable).

regimes.in_distribution: 20% trial-grouped holdout of the <2023 training period (684 contrasts); pool = remaining 80%
regimes.temporal_2023plus: pool = all <2023 (3,422), test = results posted 2023+ (1,020 contrasts / 740 trials)
regimes.loao: pool = all binary contrasts (both periods) not in the area; test = all contrasts in the held-out area

interpretation: Nominal 90% is met in-distribution by both recipes and both interval types (0.906-0.923; CIs cover 0.90).

Under the temporal 2023+ shift coverage falls to 0.83-0.86 for every recipe/interval; every 95% trial-bootstrap CI excludes 0.90. Mean widths are unchanged (~0.5-0.6 on the risk-difference scale) because calibration never sees the shifted period, so the failure is a coverage miss, not width inflation.

Leave-one-area-out coverage ranges 0.75-0.95 across recipes and interval types: over-covers on cardiometabolic/oncology (all four rows above 0.90), under-covers on 'other' (0.75-0.83) and immune/inflammatory (0.80-0.86); the interval is calibrated to the pooled mix, not to the target area.

Normalized intervals are narrower (by 0.02-0.18 in mean width) but lose 0.6-8.4 coverage points relative to constant width under shift (largest loss: 'other' area, split recipe, 8.4 pp); heteroscedastic scaling does not repair shift-induced miscoverage.

Honest cross-fitted sigma ranks errors much better than the in-sample sigma of the split recipe (in-distribution MAE at 10% coverage 0.040 vs 0.068; temporal 0.056 vs 0.090), so selective-prediction results should be read from the crossfit recipe.

Answer-or-abstain (crossfit): to hold MAE<=0.10 on answered contrasts the model can answer 88% of in-distribution contrasts (90% of trials) but only 50% of 2023+ contrasts (51% of trials); at MAE<=0.08, 61% (65% of trials) in-distribution vs 23% (25% of trials) temporal.
caveats: Single seed (0) for split assignment and model fits; crossfit CV+-style intervals lack a finite-sample exchangeability guarantee.
LOAO pools both time periods; 'other' is a heterogeneous residual category (1,634 contrasts) and its under-coverage partly reflects that.

Operating-point fractions use the largest sigma-ranked prefix whose cumulative MAE meets the target; cumulative MAE is not monotone and the threshold is chosen on the test set itself, so it is an optimistic oracle operating point, not a deployable rule.
